html:
Prussia was a German state that began as a duchy on the south-east Baltic in 1525 and grew into the kingdom that united Germany. On the map from 1530 to 1715 it is only the duchy around Königsberg; in 1783 to 1815 it is a great power stretching across northern Germany, with lands on the Rhine.

It began when the last grand master of the Teutonic Knights, Albert, turned Lutheran and made the order's land a duchy under the Polish king. In 1618 it passed by inheritance to the Hohenzollern electors of Brandenburg, and Berlin became the centre. The Great Elector freed the duchy from Polish overlordship in 1657, and his son crowned himself King in Prussia in 1701.

The kingdom was built around its army:

  • Frederick William I, the Soldier King, built a large, drilled army and paid for it with a thrifty state.
  • Frederick the Great seized Silesia in 1740 and held it through the Seven Years' War.
  • Prussia took Polish lands in the partitions of Poland.

Napoleon crushed Prussia at Jena in 1806. It reformed its state and army, and introduced compulsory schooling, fought at Waterloo, and in 1815 gained the Rhineland and much of Saxony. Under Bismarck it beat Austria and France and in 1871 made its king emperor of Germany. The Allies abolished Prussia in 1947.
